overallAssessment.verdict: The north-wales.ts file is structurally sound and covers the key facts, activities, and local character of the region with broadly accurate geography. However it carries four material blockers: (1) the hero image north-wales-hero.jpg has no provenance record and cannot be published with unknown licensing; (2) all pricing in topExperiences is from the Feb 2025 vintage likely AI-sourced set (same issue as other region files of that vintage); (3) keyFacts describes Zip World Velocity 2 as the 'World's fastest zip line' while topExperiences correctly calls it 'Europe's fastest' — 'world's fastest' is factually incorrect and a high-visibility SEO claim; (4) the markdown file uses the slug 'north-wales-coast' while the TS data file uses 'north-wales', creating a routing conflict. The Adventure Parc Snowdonia / Surf Snowdonia naming is inconsistent within the file (the venue rebranded). The hiddenGems section lists Puffin Island as a North Wales gem despite it being an Anglesey feature already covered on that region page.
overallAssessment.structuralQuality: GOOD — the TS data file covers heroContent (3 paragraphs), keyFacts (10), bestFor (10 activities), seasonGuide (4 seasons), insiderTips (8), topExperiences (8), FAQs (4), hiddenGems (3), localEatsAndDrinks (3), and SEO meta.
overallAssessment.factualConfidence: MEDIUM — core geography, heritage designations, and broad activity offer are well-established. 'World's fastest zip line' claim is incorrect. Pricing, slug consistency, and hero image provenance need human resolution before publishing.

walesCoastPath_870miles.claim: Part of 870-mile Wales Coast Path, Prestatyn to Anglesey section
walesCoastPath_870miles.verdict: VERIFIED — The Wales Coast Path totals approximately 870 miles (1,400 km) and runs the entire Welsh coastline. It begins at Chepstow in the south and terminates at Queensferry in the north, with Prestatyn as the northern trailhead for the section commonly described as the 'start' by walkers going south-to-north. The North Wales section covers the coast from Prestatyn westward to Anglesey.

zipWorld_velocitySpeed.verdict: FACTUALLY INCORRECT — Zip World Velocity 2 at Penrhyn Quarry (Bethesda) is marketed as 'the fastest zip line in Europe', not the world. The world's fastest distinction has been associated with zip lines in South Africa and the USA. topExperiences in the same file correctly states 'Europe's fastest zip—100mph over a flooded quarry.' This is an internal inconsistency where keyFacts overstates the claim.
zipWorld_velocitySpeed.action: CORRECTION REQUIRED — update keyFacts[3].detail from 'World's fastest zip line at 100mph' to 'Europe's fastest zip line at up to 100mph'. The 100mph speed figure is consistent with Zip World's own marketing. Verify current marketed top speed at the official page.
zipWorld_velocitySpeed.confidence: HIGH — 'world's fastest' is incorrect; 'Europe's fastest' is the verified claim

riverDee_gradeRapids.claim: River Dee, Llangollen — Grade 3-4 rapids, rafting and kayaking
riverDee_gradeRapids.verdict: VERIFIED — The River Dee at Llangollen is a well-established white-water venue. The Llangollen section offers Grade 3-4 whitewater and is used by multiple licensed operators for rafting and kayaking. British Canoe Union (now British Canoeing) grade the Llangollen stretch accordingly.

adventureParcSnowdonia_dolgarrog.verdict: VERIFIED — Adventure Parc Snowdonia (formerly Surf Snowdonia) is located at Dolgarrog in the Conwy Valley. The inland surf lagoon operates year-round. The venue rebranded from 'Surf Snowdonia' to 'Adventure Parc Snowdonia' in 2021 following the addition of new activities beyond surfing. NOTE: The TS file uses 'Surf Snowdonia' in topExperiences[4].name but 'Adventure Parc Snowdonia' in keyFacts[5].label — this internal inconsistency needs resolution. The correct current trading name is Adventure Parc Snowdonia.

menaiStrait_14miles.verdict: APPROXIMATELY CORRECT — The Menai Strait is approximately 25km (15.5 miles) long. '14 miles' understates the length slightly. Width varies from about 200m to 3km. The description as a kayaking venue is accurate — multiple operators including Plas Menai National Outdoor Centre run guided sessions.
menaiStrait_14miles.action: Consider updating to '~15 miles' for greater accuracy, or rephrase to avoid a specific distance claim.
menaiStrait_14miles.confidence: MEDIUM — directionally correct; minor precision issue

conwyCastle_UNESCO.claim: Conwy — UNESCO-listed castle and town walls
conwyCastle_UNESCO.verdict: VERIFIED — Conwy Castle and the medieval town walls are part of the 'Castles and Town Walls of King Edward in Gwynedd' UNESCO World Heritage Site (WHS reference 374, inscribed 1986). Along with Beaumaris, Caernarfon, and Harlech.

airports_1to2hours.claim: Liverpool and Manchester airports — 1-2 hours drive
airports_1to2hours.verdict: APPROXIMATELY CORRECT — Liverpool John Lennon Airport to Llandudno is approximately 1h15m to 1h45m by car (60-70 miles via A55). Manchester Airport to Llandudno is approximately 1h30m to 2h depending on traffic (via A55). The range '1-2 hours' is broadly accurate but Manchester to western points (Bangor, Caernarfon) can approach 2h15m in peak traffic.
airports_1to2hours.action: Claim is acceptable as written. Could be slightly more specific: 'Liverpool Airport 1-1.5 hours, Manchester Airport 1.5-2 hours' but existing broad range is not misleading.

trainAccess_underFourHours.claim: heroContent: 'trains arrive from London in under four hours'; FAQs: '3.5-4 hours from London'
trainAccess_underFourHours.verdict: PARTIALLY ACCURATE — The fastest Avanti West Coast London Euston to Llandudno Junction services take approximately 3h50m to 4h10m depending on stops. 'Under four hours' is achievable on the fastest services but not typical. '3.5-4 hours' in the FAQ is slightly optimistic — 3.5 hours to Llandudno Junction is possible on the fastest non-stop-to-Chester services, but most travellers will experience 3h45m to 4h15m. London to Bangor takes approximately 3h30m to 3h50m on direct services.
trainAccess_underFourHours.action: MINOR — Rephrase heroContent to 'trains arrive from London in around four hours' and update FAQ to '3.5-4.5 hours from London depending on service and destination' to avoid the impression that sub-4-hour service is standard.
trainAccess_underFourHours.confidence: MEDIUM — directionally correct but slightly optimistic

greatOrme_bronzeAgeMines.claim: Great Orme limestone headland — cable car, tramway, copper mines
greatOrme_bronzeAgeMines.verdict: VERIFIED — The Great Orme is a limestone headland in Llandudno. The Great Orme Bronze Age Copper Mines are one of the largest known Bronze Age copper mines in the world, open to visitors year-round. The Great Orme Tramway (opened 1902, only surviving cable-hauled tramway on public roads in Britain) and the Great Orme Country Park aerial cable car are both operational visitor attractions.

bounceBelow_176yearOld.claim: topExperiences[3]: 'Bounce Below — Trampoline through a 176-year-old slate cavern'
bounceBelow_176yearOld.verdict: OUTDATED — Llechwedd Slate Caverns (Zip World Llechwedd) opened for quarrying in 1846. The file was last updated in Feb 2025. As of 2025, the caverns were approximately 179 years old; in 2026 they are approximately 180 years old. '176-year-old' was likely accurate when first written (around 2022) but has aged. Additionally, as of July 2021, the Slate Landscape of Northwest Wales (which includes Llechwedd) was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site — this is a positive fact worth adding to the heritage positioning.
bounceBelow_176yearOld.action: Update to 'almost 180-year-old slate cavern' or simply remove the specific age in favour of 'historic Victorian slate cavern'. Consider adding UNESCO WHS reference for the Slate Landscape inscription.
bounceBelow_176yearOld.confidence: HIGH — age figure is now outdated

topBlockers.blocker: keyFacts 'World's fastest zip line' claim is factually incorrect — a high-visibility error on a commercially-sensitive claim about the region's headline attraction
topBlockers.detail: data/regions/north-wales.ts keyFacts[3].detail states 'World's fastest zip line at 100mph'. Zip World Velocity 2 is marketed as 'the fastest zip line in Europe', not the world. The TS file itself is internally inconsistent: topExperiences[0].description correctly says 'Europe's fastest zip'. Publishing 'World's fastest' when the operator's own current marketing says 'Europe's fastest' is both factually wrong and exposes Adventure Wales to credibility challenges from informed users. Zip World's official page should be verified before the copy is updated.
topBlockers.resolution: Verify current Zip World marketing at https://www.zipworld.co.uk/adventure/detail/velocity2, then update keyFacts[3].detail to 'Europe's fastest zip line at up to 100mph'. Ensure topExperiences[0].description is kept consistent. No other fact-check is needed for this specific fix.
